Stores the depth ($z$) of the closest primitive rendered to each pixel by this processor.
**Local Image Buffer:** An array of size $W \times H$.
Stores the RGB color of the closest primitive.
**Composite Z-Buffer:** An array of size $W \times H$.

*   **Bits 63–24 (40 bits):** Depth value ($z$).
*   **Bits 23–0 (24 bits):** RGB color value.
*   Distribute the atom list among $P$ processors.
*   Project the sphere onto the image plane.
*   Rasterize the sphere (or its tessellation approximation).
*   For each pixel covered by the sphere, calculate the depth $z_{local}$.
*   Perform a global reduction on the Z-buffer across all processors using the **minimum** operator.
*   Result is stored in `Composite_Z_Buffer`.
*   Each processor iterates over its local pixels.
*   If $Z_{local}^{(p)}[i] == Z_{global}[i]$, the pixel is visible (closest).
*   Otherwise, the pixel is obscured by a closer pixel on another processor.
*   Perform a global reduction on the Image buffer across all processors using the **maximum** operator.
*   Result is stored in `Composite_Image_Buffer`.
*   If the dataset does not fit in memory, read the next portion of atoms.

The subsequent maximum reduction (step 5) will select one color.
If colors are identical, the result is correct.
